name: empty
why: an empty target set is never dispatched (§6.2), but the digest of one is still defined and an encoder that special-cases the empty list is a common bug

name: many_cidrs
why: the ordinary case: a canonical, sorted, minimal list as `canonical_targets` produces it

name: unsorted_order
why: THE POINT OF THE WHOLE FILE. `scope_digest` hashes the list AS GIVEN and deliberately does not sort. An agent that sorted before hashing would compute a different digest for this input, refuse a legitimate job -- or worse, agree by luck on the sorted cases and stop checking anything on the unsorted ones

name: sorted_counterpart
why: the same three entries in sorted order. Its digest MUST differ from `unsorted_order`; the Go test asserts that inequality directly

name: duplicate_entries
why: a repeated entry is not collapsed: the list is hashed as given

name: ipv6
why: IPv6 is stored, documented and reconciled but never ENUMERATED (§0.5) -- `create_sweep` refuses an IPv6 subnet before signing. The digest is still defined over one, and the lowercase, compressed rendering `str(IPv6Network)` produces is what must be hashed byte-for-byte

name: mixed_families
why: v4 and v6 in one list, v4 first, exactly as `_canonical` orders them

name: single_addresses
why: /32 and /128 host routes: the shortest and longest well-formed entries

name: comma_collision_pair
why: ['a','b'] vs ['a,b'] -- the collision the JSON encoding exists to stop, and precisely a scope-WIDENING confusion: a digest that concatenated with a separator would let one crafted entry stand in for two authorized ones

name: comma_collision_single
why: the other half of the pair above, as ONE entry containing a comma. Its digest must differ from `comma_collision_pair`

name: quote_and_backslash
why: not a CIDR any server would send, and that is the point: the agent hashes what ARRIVED. A string escaper that differs from Python's would refuse a legitimate job or accept a mangled one

name: control_characters
why: Python escapes every C0 control, uses the short forms \b \t \n \f \r, and lowercase \u00xx for the rest -- and with ensure_ascii=True it ALSO escapes DEL (0x7f), which `canonical_bytes` does not

name: non_ascii_target
why: THE DIVERGENCE. `json.dumps` here is ensure_ascii=TRUE, so this is \u00e9 -- while `canonical_bytes` (ensure_ascii=False) would emit raw UTF-8. Reusing the agent's canonical encoder for this digest, which the plan told the builder to do, produces a different hash

name: astral_target
why: a non-BMP codepoint becomes a SURROGATE PAIR under ensure_ascii=True: \ud83d\ude00, lowercase hex, two escapes for one rune

name: u2028_u2029
why: Go's encoding/json escapes U+2028/U+2029 even with SetEscapeHTML false; Python-with-ensure_ascii escapes them too, but as part of escaping everything above 0x7e rather than as a special case

name: html_characters
why: encoding/json escapes < > & to \u003c \u003e \u0026 unless SetEscapeHTML(false); Python escapes none of them

name: empty_string_entry
why: an empty entry is below the schema's minLength 7 and can never be signed -- but the digest of a mangled list is exactly what the agent computes when deciding to REFUSE, so it has to be right

name: max_length_entry
why: 43 characters is the schema's maxLength for one target: a full IPv6 address with a prefix length
